items.title: Cost meter — usage against the WEEKLY PLAN ALLOWANCE, plus per-lane dollars
items.note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-21: 'pace ourselves based on the weekly budget for the $200 Max plan -- 10% of the weekly budget a day, so we leave a wide margin for error or unexpected needs.' 10%/day x 7 = 70% of the weekly allowance, 30% margin. [!] THIS CHANGES WHAT THIS ITEM MEASURES AND THE CHANGE IS NOT COSMETIC. A subscription plan's constraint is a WEEKLY USAGE ALLOWANCE, not a dollar spend. Every cost_usd figure in the plan (the $125 across two resumed lanes, the $11.88 in ten minutes) is API-EQUIVALENT PRICING read off session metadata -- the right signal for COMPARING lanes, the wrong denominator for PACING against a plan. Report usage-against-allowance as the budget line, keep dollars beside it as the per-lane comparison. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND MUST NOT BE INVENTED: the exact weekly allowance is not readable from this repo. FIRST JOB is to establish it from whatever surface reports plan usage, or from the operator, and to report `unknown` rather than substitute a figure until it has. A fabricated denominator under a real rule is worse than no meter. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS ESTABLISHED 2026-09-21, AND IT IS A PERCENTAGE, NOT A TOKEN COUNT. The operator read Settings > Usage directly. Plan: Max (20x). The surface exposes THREE meters, each a percent-of-allowance bar with no absolute number anywhere: a ~5-hour SESSION window, a WEEKLY window, and a SEPARATE WEEKLY LIMIT FOR FABLE. Anthropic's own support pages publish no figure either -- only '20x Pro per-session allowance'. [!] DO NOT CONVERT TO TOKENS, and this is a design decision rather than a limitation. The allowance is MODEL-WEIGHTED, so tokens-per-percent is not a constant -- it is a function of the model mix and moves whenever the manager routes a lane to sonnet instead of opus. A token budget would read as precise and drift silently. A1 METERS IN PERCENT. The operator's rule -- 10% of the weekly budget per day -- is already stated in that unit, so no conversion is needed to enforce it. A measured per-model exchange rate may be reported as a sanity check, labelled measured and drifting, NEVER as the budget. [!] TWO WINDOWS BIND, NOT ONE. The weekly cap is what the 10%/day rule governs; the ~5-hour session window is what actually walls a lane mid-run. A day's 10% spent as a single burst can exhaust the session window while the weekly meter still reads green, so A1 MUST SHOW BOTH or it reports 'fine' during an outage. [!] MEASURED 2026-09-21, and it CORRECTS an earlier claim on this row that was asserted rather than checked. The claim was that a meter summing only agent lanes would systematically under-report because the operator's own chat draws on the same pool. The mechanism is real -- all surfaces do share one limit -- but the magnitude is currently ZERO: 'What's using your week' reads Claude Code 100%, Chats 0%, Cowork 0%, Other 0%. Lane accounting is therefore ~= the whole pool today. A1 should still LABEL its scope, because the day that mix changes the meter goes quietly wrong. [!] THE MANAGER'S METER IS THE **DAILY** BUDGET, NOT THE WEEKLY BAR (operator, 2026-09-21): 'the manager should be focused on the daily budget, not weekly, as I sometimes use Claude for other projects... I will start a new manager session after this one and I expect it to use the daily budget, even if we pass into the margin.' [!] THIS CORRECTS A CLAIM WRITTEN ON THIS ROW EARLIER THE SAME DAY, and it is the SAME CATEGORY ERROR this row already caught once with cost_usd. That claim read: '68% of the week consumed with ~2 of 7 days left, ~13.6%/day against a 10%/day target, so THE STATED POLICY IS NOT BEING MET.' It compared TOTAL weekly consumption against the MANAGER'S daily allowance -- two different populations. The weekly bar aggregates every surface and every project the operator touches, including work this repo's manager cannot see and did not cause, so it CANNOT grade the manager. ('Claude Code 100%' does not rescue it: the operator's other projects are also Claude Code.) The 68% reading stands as a fact about the ACCOUNT; the conclusion drawn from it was unsupported and is withdrawn. [!] SO A1 REPORTS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND MUST NOT BLEND THEM. (a) THE CONTROL VARIABLE: this repo's spend today against the daily budget -- 10% of the weekly allowance. That is the number the manager is accountable for. (b) CONTEXT ONLY: the account-level weekly bar, unattributable and reported as such. A single blended 'budget' figure is the bug. [!] THE 30% WEEKLY MARGIN IS NOT A RESERVE THE MANAGER PRESERVES BY DOING LESS. It exists to absorb the operator's other projects and surprises. A manager that throttles its own lane because the ACCOUNT bar looks high is spending the margin's purpose on nothing. The operator has stated explicitly that the next manager should spend its daily budget EVEN IF that passes into the margin. [!] AND THE FAILURE MODE IS NOT HITTING A CAP -- it is 'losing work to sessions dying in the middle' (operator). THAT IS A DURABILITY PROBLEM, NOT A BUDGET ONE, and budgeting alone cannot fix it. The mitigations are structural: land work in small PRs rather than one large one, push before you answer, and keep state on disk (PIPELINE.jsonl, the checklist) rather than in a session's head. The ~5-HOUR SESSION WINDOW is what actually kills a session mid-task, so it is the in-session number to watch; the weekly bar never killed anything mid-run. [!] FABLE HAS A SEPARATE WEEKLY ALLOWANCE, MEASURED AT 0% USED, AND THE OPERATOR HAS DIRECTED THAT IT BE EMPLOYED (2026-09-21): 'it should definitely be used when appropriate -- we want to employ that budget as well, we just want to make sure it is getting the tasks that are the best use of that resource.' It is a SECOND pool that does not draw on the main one, so work routed there is additive capacity, not a trade-off. That makes it a live routing input for the model table in .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md. Tracked as E11 -- A1 reports the pool, E11 decides what goes in it. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 alongside A3a rather than before it, because A3a was told to render section 5 WITHOUT the spend figures (it already has the unrouted count from pipeline.py) and to print an explicit 'not measured -- A1 not built' line. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 on OPUS: it edits config on accounts that trade, and although the mirror is paper, the roster it must match is alpaca_live's, which is real money. If the roster edit lands in those tiers it lands the Tier-1 half, states the exact one-line change, and STOPS — and it was told explicitly that leaving the new test RED against current config is a legitimate outcome that makes the gap loud, while weakening the test to go green is not. items.note: OPERATOR GRANT 2026-09-21, verbatim: 'All the ladder decisions can be automated -- that is a standing mandate. Strategies can be promoted to live money without explicit operator approval if the evidence supports the decision. I should just get a ping in realtime of the update and an evidence review in the next daily briefing.' FIVE MANDATES ARE GRANTED: MD-PROMOTE-S0-S1, MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 (REAL MONEY), MD-DEMOTE-S2-S1, MD-DEMOTE-S1-OFF, MD-KILL-QUESTION. Build config/mandates.yaml + the resolver + the ping + the section-1 evidence render. [!] THE FILE IS NOT CREATED AHEAD OF THE RESOLVER -- a config nothing reads is the 'declared capability with no consumer' antipattern this repo already names. [!] WHAT CARRIES THE SAFETY IS 'if the evidence supports it': a COMMITTED evidence record, named harness, stated n, net of the FULL cost stack, clearing a rule registered before the run. A claim in a PR body is not a record; B1 is what makes that checkable. [!] MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 MUST NOT ARM UNTIL D1 LANDS -- arithmetic, not caution: the harnesses default slippage and funding to 0.0, so every 'passed the backtest' verdict in today's corpus is fee-only and optimistic by an unknown amount (+0.57R on the one leg measured). The derisk_only mandates carry no such block; they read live measurement, not the corpus. Bounds and the bar's content are operator decisions -- plan open decisions 5 and 6. [!] THE BAR AND THE CAP ARE NOW DECIDED (2026-09-21), so B5 builds against fixed numbers rather than waiting on them. BAR, all three clauses: expectancy > 0 net of the FULL cost stack at n >= 30 closed; positive in a MAJORITY of walk-forward folds; Stage-1 realized cost within a stated tolerance of modelled cost. CAP: total declared risk across AUTO-PROMOTED legs <= 25% of the account's configured risk budget, and NO RATE LIMIT -- a leg-per-week cap was offered and declined, so a batch CAN land in one day and the 25% number is load-bearing on its own. items.title: armed-branch-push-watch races PR creation — every post-merge follow-up trips it
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-21 on PR #12673, which is the follow-up to the reset's own merge. scripts/ci/check_armed_branch_push.py reported `dropped` (error, exit 1) on a HEALTHY push. Timing is the whole bug: #12668 squash-merged as 3ea2777 at 12:18 and GitHub deleted the branch; the branch was reset from the new main and A6 pushed at 12:25:43; #12673 was opened at 12:26:10. The watcher ran in that 27-second gap, when the branch's ONLY associated PR was the merged #12668 whose head.sha (1d596e2) is not the pushed sha (f3301d0). [!] THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF. A PR cannot be opened for a branch that has not been pushed, so EVERY follow-up PR made the sanctioned way (git fetch origin main && git checkout -B <branch> origin/main) trips this between push and PR creation. The guard's premise -- that the PR it finds is the PR for this push -- is false during a branch reset. [!] DO NOT 'FIX' IT BY DOWNGRADING THE SEVERITY. The loss it exists for (#11846) is real, and a guard that cries wolf on the healthy path is how a guard gets ignored -- the desensitisation this repo already measured at 202 of 376 CRITICALs being one un-latched condition. Sharpen the condition. [!] THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it does NOT fall into the ancestry trap the script's own docstring warns about. That trap is asking whether a BRANCH commit reached main -- which a squash merge always answers no to. Ask the OPPOSITE: is the old PR's MERGE COMMIT an ancestor of the PUSHED commit? Branch correctly reset -> yes (3ea2777 is an ancestor of f3301d0), nothing lost, a new PR is coming. Genuine drop, i.e. more commits pushed onto the merged branch's old history -> no; the pre-merge head is the ancestor instead. A squash does not defeat that direction. [!] The script has an elaborate --self-test with a mutation-tested exact-sha comparison; extend it rather than loosening it, and add the branch-reset case as a NAMED fixture so the next person cannot re-introduce this by tightening something else. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21, sonnet-5, fresh, ceiling $12 (this row carried no ceiling; one is set now). It earns its slot today because the manager's own pushes are the population it mis-grades: every follow-up PR made the sanctioned way trips it in the gap between push and PR creation. Lane told in terms to SHARPEN the condition and NOT downgrade the severity, and to CONSTRUCT both cases rather than implement the proposed discriminator on trust -- a reported hole beats a confident fix. [!] CLOSED 2026-09-21 AS ALREADY FIXED, AND THE LANE THAT ESTABLISHED IT WAS DISPATCHED IN ERROR BY THIS MANAGER. The fix landed in #12676 -- the SAME PR the handoff named as 'A7's pipeline + close-out contract + E10' -- and this row was never moved off `queued`. VERIFIED on main, not taken from the lane: scripts/ci/check_armed_branch_push.py defines RESET_FROM_MERGE, carries the merge-commit-ancestry discriminator, and has the branch-reset case as a named self-test fixture. Cost of the error: $0.93. [!] THE LESSON IS NOT 'READ MORE CAREFULLY', it is that a row's `state` was not moved by the PR that resolved it, so the register lied to the next reader in the direction of MORE work rather than less. Filed as PI-20260921-M06.

items.title: Employ the Fable weekly allowance — decide WHICH task classes, by measurement
items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-21, verbatim: 'it should definitely be used when appropriate -- we want to employ that budget as well, we just want to make sure it is getting the tasks that are the best use of that resource.' Do not read a task list into this row that is not here. [!] FIRST FABLE ROUTING DECIDED AND DISPATCHED 2026-09-21, and the class chosen is GREP-AND-CLASSIFY SWEEP OVER A REPOSITORY. Chosen by this row's own stated method -- 'start with a class whose output is cheaply verifiable against work a current-model lane has already done, diff the two, and widen only on that evidence' -- so the probe runs IN PARALLEL with E9's sonnet sweep over the same needle set, and the diff is the measurement.
